a.title: The answer

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: The answer: a layer of software between every program and the

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: hardware. Seen from three sides, it is a virtual machine (it

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: turns the physical machine into a nicer virtual one), a standard

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: library (it offers system calls), and a resource manager (it

a.title: The answer

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: The answer: the OS switches the processor among them so fast that

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: each believes it owns one. The switch is the mechanism; the

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: choice of who runs next is the policy. A process is a running

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: program, and in xv6 it is one struct proc that holds the

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: 3.4 Many processes on few processors, on a real

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.title: The answer

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: The answer: each process has a private address space, and the OS

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: maps it onto a different part of physical memory, with the

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: hardware translating every access. Private memory is also how a

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: bug in one program stays in that program.
